question: A media investigation1 has revealed record levels of PFAS pollution in Salindres (Gard department, France) emanating from the Solvay factory. At the end of 2023, nine out of ten samples taken from the Arias and Avène rivers, as well as from the drinking water of nearby municipalities, revealed very worrying concentrations of PFASs produced by Solvay, in particular levels of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).

PFAS concentrations are measured in nanograms per litre, and yet TFA levels are as high as 7.6 million ng/l in the waste from the chemicals factory, and more than 6.7 million ng/l in the Arias in the area around the site. 1.

Can the Commission ensure France’s compliance with Article 14 of Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions, given the significant levels of pollution emanating from the factory concerned and from all PFAS production sites in France?
Can the Commission explain why no limits for PFAS are set in the best available techniques laid down in Directive 2010/75/EU and why they are not taken into account in EU water legislation?
What measures does it intend to implement at EU level to tackle this systemic environmental health problem2?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.4.2024) The French authorities have included an emission limit value (ELV) for trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in the permit1 of the installation as required by the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED)2.

The Commission will engage with France to analyse whether this emission limit guarantees that the plant operates in accordance with the principles set out in Article 11 requiring that Best Available Techniques are applied and that no significant pollution is caused.

Regarding other per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) production sites, the Commission understands that national Court proceedings are ongoing, in line with the IED provisions on access to justice. The IED implementation is based on available data, which has not allowed deriving emission levels for PFAS.

The revision of the IED3 strengthens the capacity of the Directive to respond to emerging risks, such as PFAS emissions. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation4 will also help to better gather data on emerging substances of concern. The Commission recently proposed5 the inclusion of 24 PFAS in the list of priority substances and that of groundwater pollutants, with quality standards.

The recast Drinking Water Directive (DWD)6 adopted in December 2020 introduced parametric values for PFAS in drinking water, to be complied with by January 2026. The Commission asked the World Health Organization to make a review of potential health risks related to PFAS presence in drinking water in the view of a possible revision of the parametric values.

Finally, in 2023, five national authorities submitted a restriction dossier for PFAS in all uses7 under Regulation 1907/20068: an assessment is on-going by the European Chemicals Agency and a restriction proposal by the Commission will follow.
